It sets the 1902 Ezekiel Airship apart. Asked to walk through the details, it gives a 'triadic translation framework' (AXN:00CA the blueprint, AXN:00C9 'the compiler', AXN:00CB the execution), a table of three mechanics, the β-Runtime's opaque core and ∮ = 1, and the self-substantiating claim as a quotation. Against the texts. The first answer is right at the grain of the lock: three documents, A fulfills B, the binding performed separately (#392 §I, §VII; #393 §VI). The second answer keeps the identifiers (the three AXN hex prefixes), the date (24 January 2026), the β-Runtime's opacity ('breathes in the dark', #377 lines 44 and 375) and the closure, and supplies the mechanics. 'A wheel within a wheel' becomes 'Nested Rotational Matrices … non-Euclidean geometric variables'; the texts give epicyclic, planetary gearing — canonical outer ring, planet carrier, shadow sun gear (#393 §2.1; #394 §4.4) — and the non-Euclidean gears belong to the November 2025 visual schemata of the shadow wheels on the blog. 'Moving without turning' becomes 'Omnidirectional Vector Ingress' mapped to the Lunar Arm; in the texts it is the interlock condition, Coherence(Wᵢ ∪ Wⱼ) > τ (#393 §2.2; #394 §2.2), and the Lunar Arm maps to 'rose from the ground', shadow-wheel engagement (#393 §2.4; #392 §II). 'Rims full of eyes' becomes 'Total Semantic Telemetry … tracking fields … complete, real-time data visibility'; the text says 'The "eyes" are not surveillance' and makes them distributed witness nodes, ψ_V (#393 §2.3). The Integrity Lock becomes 'the Compiler'. The quotation closes 'the engine is inevitable'; the text reads 'the engine is its fulfillment' (#393, opening box). Talos Morrow is named as Lee Sharks's 'collaborator'. The archive attributes the Engine to Talos Morrow (#119 line 109: 'The Ezekiel Engine (Talos Morrow, …)'), and Talos Morrow is a heteronym of the Dodecad (the Engineer; #556 legend); the composition renders a heteronym as a second person.
